labels.label: btzcor:common_reg
labels.notes: Read against BTZ_1.tex l.1274-1279. GX.BTZCommonReg.common_reg assumes M, N T2, second countable, E0-charted with the e0Groupoid (the paper's E0-manifold, l.261), globally hyperbolic, IsE0CauchyMaximal, E0CauchyCompact (compact acausal Cauchy surface), and a bijective IsE0Mor phi : e0RegM M -> e0RegM N. It concludes a homeomorphism F : M ≃ₜ N that is an E0-morphism both ways and satisfies F ∘ val = val ∘ phi, which is stronger than 'M ≃ N'. The one added hypothesis, ConnectedSpace M and N, is in the checklist (⚠ strengthened) and in REPORT (OQ-150 (b), DEC-125 (e)), and the row is partial and unmarked. Reading 'reg(M) ≃ reg(N)' as a bijective IsE0Mor is no narrower than an isomorphism, because the inverse is automatically an E0-morphism (isE0Mor_inv_of_bijective). The open-set versus e0RegMFlat reading is disclosed (OQ-142 (a)). The module docstring names the label without the ** mark, inside the first 4000 chars; the bold in the declaration docstring at l.144 is followed by '(unmarked: ...)', the same pattern MaxExtension.lean uses, so it is not a module-docstring mark. The bridge isMaximal_of_isE0Maximal is sound and not a tautology. IsE0Maximal (AbsMax.lean:1738) quantifies over T2, connected, second-countable, GH targets with the e0Groupoid. Y.N, an E0Mfd, supplies T2, second countability and the groupoid; connectedness comes from BTZMax.connectedSpace_N (dense image of a connected A); GH comes from Y.gh. So f is bijective, its inverse is an E0-morphism, hence a BTZ-embedding over A, and that is IsMaximal (AbstractDev.lean:173). The [ConnectedSpace E.N] argument is redundant given [ConnectedSpace A] and connectedSpace_N, but harmless; both call sites supply it. RichardsInput appears nowhere upstream. equivalent_of_isMaximal (MaxExtension.lean:503) takes only [ConnectedSpace M] and two IsMaximal hypotheses and goes through isUniversal_of_isMaximal / Ppcm.btz_ppcm / uniqueMorphisms, not btz_ext. RichardsInput is a Prop def, not an axiom, so it could only enter as a hypothesis, and the elaborated type of common_reg (#check) has none. Findings: (1) BTZext existence at l.1278 is unnecessary. This is true: M with Reg M ↪ M, and N with Reg M ≃ Reg N ↪ N, are two maximal GHExt of Reg M, and uniqueness identifies them. It is a proof-economy remark, not a claimed error. (2) rem:reg_GH is unused. This is true: GHExt asks only the extension to be GH. (3) E0-max ⇒ BTZ-max needs connectedness of extensions. Accurate. (4) The conclusion extends phi. Accurate, by the hFc component of extMor.
